utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. I'm sorry that I was responsible for the circumstances that have led to a late start this morning. Your affirmation still applies, sir. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness Ostreni.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown the map, P515, page 3, admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I, once again, be asked about the participation of the NLA from -- members from Albania, because I don't think I heard the question well and I don't think I gave the right answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski, if you'll excuse me. May I ask you, again, sir, about the participation of the Albanian representatives in the NLA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. There were members. But the way I understood your question was whether I knew them or not, and that's why I answer in that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski, you may want to follow that up. That's a matter for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness Ostreni, is it correct that there were NLA members who were Albanian nationals?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. There were some.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: As far as I remember, you replied that you knew at least one of them.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because I thought whether you asked me whether I knew one of them, and I'm still repeating that I used to know one of them who was killed on the 12th [as interpreted]. This is the reason why I asked the -- His Honour to ask me the question again, to answer to his question.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please tell me which month it was, the 12th of which month, to be precise, for the transcript to be precise?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't -- I didn't use the term "12th." I said that there were Albanian citizens, nationals, in the NLA ranks.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You stated that - that is in line 14: "I knew one of them who was killed on the 12th."

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant Brigade 112th, to make it clear for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Do you see the map in front of you? You have it also in hard copy.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It's a map of Brigade 113.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You stated that you have marked it.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This is the territory under the control of the NLA in 2001?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This is the area around the city of Kumanovo.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: More specifically, it is the area to the west of Kumanovo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see that from the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Considering that the map does not end with a blue line on the left side, could you explain if this is the end or the border of the territory that was under the control of the 112th Brigade; or, to be clearer, the territory under the control of the 113th Brigade, did it extend beyond this map, beyond where this map ends, or is interrupted?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are saying on the left. Do you mean the western part of the map? I didn't mark it. I marked only the eastern part which was engaged in daily fighting with the army and the police forces. That must have been marked by the General Staff of the army. That's why NATO was happy with this line. Within this line, in the west, there is the -- there is Brigade 113 and the newly established 112th Brigade. But for NATO, it was important to have the -- to have marked the line where the monitors could observe the observance of cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see where the map ends on the left-hand side? It ends in the left-hand side without any marking. Does it mean that also the territory that cannot be seen in this map was under the control of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can be seen in the operational plan, that I have submitted to the Court, the location of the units and so on. But in this case, the aim was to highlight the front line of the brigade and to set two borders: The state border in the north and the south-western border of the brigade as the zone of its responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When you're talking about another map, that would be the map that we had seen, together with the instructions, the one marked in yellow where the territory under the NLA control was marked in yellow. Were you referring to that one?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I believe you know that in the north-western part, there were units of the army of the Republic of Macedonia, units from the 1st Brigade, which -- and also units from the police battalion in the north-western part, which operated in the direction of Slupcane and Orizare and these villages, during MX-1 and MX-2 and later operation called Vaksince, trying to break up the defence line and get together. But they failed to realise that during the fighting, so I have marked the part or the area where our forces were deployed. The army must have marked its own location in the north-western part and outside this border. For me, it was important to mark the battery that was here, above Alasec. I didn't mark the location of other forces because they were not undertaking operations before the attack started from Kumanovo direction. They always acted in cooperation with the operational tactical group number 2. They were part of a tactical group number 1, but that is a question of the use of forces. In this map, you see the outline of the territory, the first part, and the lining of our units. At the time NATO didn't ask us to give it details, because they wanted this information to know about the cease-fire. They weren't interested in further details related to the units, but only the area under our responsibility. So NATO was content with the information provided it with.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see in the lowest part of the map, in the lowest part on the left-hand side, that the -- there is a marking with an interrupted black and blue line? The black line consists of semi-circles.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is done based on the rules, on the content of the maps. May I answer the question, because sometimes I may hurry up because I understand the language that the question is being put to me. May I continue, Your Honour? I know very well the Macedonian language, Your Honour, and sometimes I maybe hurry up in answering and don't wait for the translation. I apologise for that. The line that you are asking me is done in conformity with the then rules on the drawing of the maps and represents the border of the area of responsibility on the right side of the brigades that were deployed there, 113 and 114.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does this line end here; or, if the map would continue, would the line also continue following the same direction?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a question about which I make suppositions. You're asking me whether the map would continue. The map doesn't continue, so that's the information I've provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether the line, the line that I asked you about previously, the one marked with intermittent black semi-circular and blue lines, continues beyond this section of the map.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would continue, depending on where the area of responsibility of the brigade would be. It would normally continue on that line or in that direction, but it would be a mere supposition. So I'm saying and answering about things I have done in real terms, what I draw from the general map, in consultation with the commander of Brigade 113.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you have any other map where it is marked where this line would continue?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only on the map of operations, if it's there; but, otherwise, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you have a map that you have marked, a map that you would have had provided to NATO about the borders, the lines of delineation, in the areas of Ljubanci and Ljuboten, since in this map here, we can see Matejce that was under the control of the 113th Brigade and 114th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall to have submitted any other map to NATO, other than the current one. I don't remember. I think I don't have given anything else; but to tell you the truth, I don't remember. I know that I didn't work with many maps, also because for -- for reasons of maintaining the secret of my duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see the city of Kumanovo in the map?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the NLA was never waging a war to -- to conquer Kumanovo?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that the NLA has been -- came so far to the line that you see here until the cease-fire, and didn't undertake any operation outside this line in the direction of Kumanovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So the NLA never carried out combats to conquer the city of Kumanovo?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because for four months, the NLA reached as far as this level, until it reached the cease-fire of the 6th of July, and it respected the cease-fire and stopped at these positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And is it true that the NLA never penetrated to the east [as interpreted] of Kumanovo?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise the transcript is incorrect. It should be to the "south-east" of Kumanovo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please repeat the question again? I apologise for asking you to repeat it, but I want to understand it properly in order to give you a right answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct, as well, that the NLA never penetrated to the south-east of Kumanovo.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the word "penetrate" in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: He is asking the interpreter to interpret it again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The NLA penetrated until the positions marked here, with the exception of Haracin from where the battalion withdrew; but it didn't penetrate or didn't attack the other parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So, the NLA had never under its control territory to the south-east of Kumanovo?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in the south-east of Kumanovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown P515, page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see the map in front of you?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You stated that the intermittent line marks the area that was potentially under the NLA Brigade 116th, and the uninterrupted line marks the area that was under the control of the 116th Brigade of the NLA. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that, this is what I said. The intermittent line shows the possible area of responsibility because there were weapons stations a little bit far for security reasons, and then -- and then there is the area where the brigade was concentrated.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see the village of Dobri Dol in the map. It is in the upper right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the north-east, yes, Dobri Dol; if we are speaking of the same place.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes. We're speaking about the same place.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Near Pozaran [phoen], yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that Dobri Dol was not under the NLA control in 2001?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything that is situated outside the marking were not under NLA control. Dobri Dol, too - I think it is part of Gostivar commune - that, too, was not part. I have to look at the other maps. I don't know maybe it is included in the or maps; but seemingly, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And it is correct that in the areas marked as the potential and as the actual area under the control of the 116th Brigade, there is no city.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can see it. You can see it on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct -- could you tell me -- I apologise. I will reframe my question. Is it correct that the area in Skopska Crna Gora mountain, to the north of Skopje, was not comprised in the maps that you provided to the ICTY investigators as areas under the NLA control?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have submitted the maps that are now in front of me. These are the only ones I have submitted. Karadak, Montenegro, Skopje are notions, describing or representing a broader territory. I concentrated my answer on the fact that I gave these maps, and that the territory marked on them show where the NLA, its respective brigades or parts thereof or battalions, had their control. That was the summary of the answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did the ICTY investigators ask you to mark in the map the area around Ljubanci and Ljuboten that was under the NLA control?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I think you are pushing me to make some mistakes. When I was asked from the Tribunal, I gave them these maps, the same ones that we gave to NATO, and this is the territory that was under our control. If you are -- if you are pushing me towards making some errors, and including Ljuboten, Ljubanci, and I don't know what, I don't think that's the right way to put questions to me, because I think your aim is to make me go into the wrong alley. I kindly ask you to ask the questions in a clearer form, so that I can give you the right answers to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I apologise if you're thinking that I'm trying to mislead you, but I think that I asked you -- that I'm asking you straightforward questions and I expect that you can answer to, and that you are the person who knows those answers best. Is it correct, as well, that the NATO forces, when you were disarming, did not ask you to mark in the map what was the territory around Skopje that was under the NLA control?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't asked us to mark anything else other than the territory where the brigades were stationed, in their positions. NATO and others, who were part of the monitoring group, allowed -- were happy with this map because that enabled them to follow up whether the cease-fire was respected, to identify the places that might have been violated. At this time, I gave them the maps after I was consulted with the brigade commanders, and then the same maps I gave also to these commanders, for them to know to abide by the cease-fire because that was the main issue at the time for the NLA, because we had to -- talks had to start on the political agreement on the interruption of fighting and establishment of peace in the Republic of Macedonia. That was the reason why NATO asked us to give it these maps which we tried to be as precise as possible in representing the territory under the command of the brigades, then the front line, and on the right side or the south-west, the area of operation, the border of its area of operation in the case of 113 and 114 Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So you mean to say that the NATO forces were interested in the entire area, in the territory in Macedonia under the NLA control, apart from the area around the capital, Skopje. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not. What I'm saying is that they wanted us to provide them with a map with the markings that would identify the territory in which the brigades of the NLA had established their authority. They did not mention Skopje. They asked for the above. That's why, in these pieces of maps, I marked the positions where the NLA, at the time, was stationed. I will repeat myself again. This was in line with the preparations for the cease-fire, and that's why we didn't put all the details on these maps because we didn't know, at the time, whether the cease-fire would result in a political agreement, and that's why there was a need to safeguard the notes that would depict in more details the positions of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did -- was the village of Tanusevci under the control of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, the 1st ARM Brigade was operating in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please answer shortly with "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a very delicate issue. I cannot answer to it either with "yes" or "no." I will repeat myself again that, in that area, the first special brigade, the Skorpians, was operating there of the ARM, and there was a special platoon of the border units and perhaps some units of the military police. This is what I'm telling, that on that part that you're mentioning here, these were the forces operating.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But did you not answer to my question: Was the village of Tanusevci under the control of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that at the time, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In 2001, was the village of Tanusevci under the control of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The beginning of the uprising is there, then the ARM forces intervened and Tanuse remained, to my recollection, under the control of the ARM forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In what time was the village of -- or from which month was the village of Tanusevci under the control of the ARM?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the 12th, the day, but I don't remember the month. I will tell you of the case. It was when the ARM forces undertook --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: May I remind you, may I refresh your memory. Was this perhaps the month of February?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 16th of February, they intervened; but then, again, they went out to the border, met with the KFOR forces. I don't remember the month. I know that the day is 12th. So maybe it is 12th of April, but I'm not sure. The forces of this brigade then remained on that part; while on the 16th of February, there were clashes in Tanuse. However, I was not there at the time. This was reported through the media as an event that marked the beginning of the armed clashes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And you, as the Chief of the General Staff, you can't tell me when you held the village from which your uprising began under control and when the Macedonian security forces held this village under control?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I'm saying to you, sir, is that when the MX-1 operation commenced, from that time, these forces began to act on the back of 112th Brigade. I enumerated the forces that were stationed there. As for the exact date when these forces entered Tanuse, that I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that, to the investigators of the OTP, you did not give the map for the area under the control of the NLA in the area of Skopje, because the village of Ljuboten is marked as a village under the control of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are again trying to mislead me, sir. This is not true. The NLA units were never in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that no map has marked the area of -- under the control of the 111th Brigade, because such a brigade did not exist?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Physically as such, as an operative brigade, it did not function that way. The people were known. Their leader was known, but they were in their own houses because the cease-fire came into force. Our aim was not to create tension. Our aim was for everything to end in a political agreement and to put an end to the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Members of the 111th Brigade lived in their houses. This is your evidence?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But they had their persons in charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did they keep their weapons in their homes?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what they had in their homes. I and the General Staff made efforts to secure anti-tank weapons because that part, the Kercove part, was a part where there was constant movement of armoured vehicles, but we didn't manage to cross them over. These would have been the weapons that we would provide them with. However, the cease-fire came into force, things improved, the Ohrid Agreement was signed, and there was no need to activate that brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Where were the warehouses for the weapons of the 111th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 111th Brigade would have looked for support from 116 Brigade in the beginning; and, of course, later on, procurement would have taken place. As I said already, I didn't manage to provide them weapons. I don't know for each and every member of them, I only knew the -- their leaders.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did each member of the NLA have personal weaponry, a personal weapon?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which persons are you referring to? Those that were in their homes or those at positions? I want to be chore on your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm asking you about all members of the NLA of the 111th, 112th, 113th, 114th, 115th, and 116th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for 111th, that I can not say, because they were not activated. They were in their homes. As for the other brigades that I provided the positions of 112th to 116th, they had weapons, but we did not manage to provide each and every member with a weapon. So a selection took place; for example, the cooks remained without weapons. For example, for an 82-millimetre mortar, you need eight persons. These persons were not provided with personal weapons because they were positioned in the rear, and they were defended and protected by the forces on the first front line. Again, part of the soldiers in the training centres, they were not provided with weapons because, first, they had to undergo training, to get the uniforms, to start their military education. So they used one, two, three, or four weapons, to the extent they could, to do the shooting training; and, then, as the procurement occurred, that's how they were furnished with weapons. Then, the doctors, the health department, the nurses, they also were not provided with personal weapons due to the lack of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did the other brigades also have inactive members, the 112th, 113th, 114th, 115th, 116th?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not receive a good interpretation. Could you please repeat the question? I know the Macedonian language, and this is in contrary to what is said because the NLA did not have reservists. It had volunteers, and we had no idea how many volunteers will come to join in each and every brigade. So the logistic department also dealt with the personnel issue of the brigades and looked after avoiding too many volunteers joining at the same time because providing them with weapons would occur as a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown P487, received in evidence. Can we please zoom in on the map, upper middle part. Yes, this part. Can we zoom in further, please, the area around Skopje. It's in the middle of the map. Can we zoom in on this, please. A little bit further up. No. Can we just have the whole map up a little. Could we zoom in the central area which is marked with yellow. Yes, this is it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Your evidence before this Chamber was that the areas marked with yellow were under the control of the NLA. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the north-western part.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I see here the road, the highway Skopje-Velice marked in yellow. Was the highway under your control?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. The yellow colour here is of the map itself. You can see the same yellow in other areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was the area north of Skopje, marked here, was under the control of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It is the way it is marked. It's very small, but it was up to Haracin; then after the withdrawal of Haracin, the line moves to Mojance; and then from Mojance, you can see the border, the right-hand side border of the brigade, that goes up north. In fact, this is what I gave NATO, and it can be better seen in these conditions. Haracin is not depicted here because with -- we withdrew from Haracin. So you're allowed to mark with an "X" those locations that you lost or you withdraw from. So this map that we provided NATO with had to be accurate, because otherwise the monitors would find themselves in an awkward position.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You told us that NATO was not interested in the areas around Skopje, and they did not ask you to mark a map about NLA control around Skopje.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. Maybe this is the way you understood my questions [as interpreted]. What I said was NATO asked us to mark on the map the territory where the NLA had established its authority. Based on this request, launched by Peter Feith and addressed to Ali Ahmeti, I worked on these maps. I marked them, NATO collected them. And, of course, when they compared them with the maps they were provided with by the ARM, there were no remarks on part of NATO, with the exception of the units that were inside the territory. As I already mentioned, on the north-west, there were forces of the army; then in Popova Shapka, there were also ARM units. So this was sufficient for the monitors to be able to carry out their duties. So whenever there was a movement away from this line, as it happened on the 25th and 26th of July, Mr. Ali Ahmeti gave an order for the NLA forces to withdraw from their intervention in Tetovo-Jezince road. So these maps were the basis for safeguarding the cease-fire. So the requests of the monitors to both parties was to respect this border-line. There were problems also on part of the police and the ARM, but we are talking of the territories that are marked on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that Ljuboten is also marked in yellow as being under the control of the NLA on this map?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see that. What I know is that Ljuboten was never under the control of National Liberation Army. Last time, I called on these maps, too, because these maps are exact maps. So the same positions should be both on the operational map and on these maps. But on the operational one there are other colours, and it is quite possible for this colours to be mixed up. But it is how it was in reality in the map that I provided in the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that, according to this map, Tanusevci also is marked as territory under the control of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is how I depicted Kodra i Diellit, or Popova Shapka, 112th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm asking you about Tanusevci.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is how it is depicted on that map because I was getting ready to go to the east of Kumanovo, not to the west, because we were expecting risk. Those forces there would have remained isolated if the forces went towards the east of Skopje, towards Mali i Thate. So we had to prepare for the future. Our aim was not to fight against those forces because that would have caused a blood bath.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you respond to my question, whether it is correct that on this map, Tanusevci is marked as a territory under the control of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said that the entire area, as I've depicted it in yellow, at that time I was not thinking that we will come here to The Hague and discuss each village individually. So the idea of this map was to show where the NLA was holding ground and which direction it should take. Had I known at the time that I would come here to testify, I would have included more details. But now after six years, we're talking for several days on these issues. There are many dates, many issues mentioned. So you should also consider the fact that I'm a human, too, and it is difficult for me, too, to remember every date and every detail that are maybe required today here in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This map then is not truthful. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: How can it not be truthful? When you have a map, you have an operation planned, you have the task written on it, it has a stamp, a signature, and this map would be followed. But myself and everyone in the NLA were happy that this plan was not implemented and that things ended in a political agreement with the signing of the Ohrid Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Are -- is -- are the information on this map incorrect?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To me, these markings of -- on the map were enough to prepare this operation. I prepared it for the level of the NLA, for our abilities, mental and physical. This is how it was. Of course, the forces of the Tactical Group 1 on the north are not marked in the 112th Brigade because, at the time, I didn't deem them important.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the information regarding the areas marked in yellow were under -- as being under the control of the NLA is incorrect?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to be precise, I gave NATO these other maps so that the full picture was there, that everything was clear which was this territory. So the map was aimed at organising an operation. At the time, I didn't give this map to NATO. I only gave them the maps that were -- that had on them marked the current positions, and I gave them these maps on the 5th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for your answer regarding the maps. Oftentimes, in your evidence, you called upon the book of Petrovski, and you assess it as giving a reliable assessment of the situation in Macedonia in 2001. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that. I have mentioned him several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Have you read also the book, "War in Macedonia" by Mitre Arsovksi and Damjanovski?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only that I read it, but I published a book as a critical review of that book. In my book, I have laid out my views and criticism on this collective book, "The War in Macedonia 2001." In other words, I'm well familiar with this book.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You critique this book as having a lot of untruthfulness in it. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way I have written it, it embodied my belief.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But are your beliefs such that this book contains a lot of untruth, a lot of untruthful things?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The book contains political views and stance which were not put forward in a scientific manner as they should have been. One of the reasons for that is that the outcomes of what was happening in Macedonia are described by those gentlemen as causes that caused the damage to democracy in Macedonia; that is, the protest of Albanians, the demands of Albanians, everything they did from a long time ago, the demands for university in Albanian language, their demands for respect for their national symbols. All these things are decked out there as causes that -- that destroyed the state of Macedonia. In fact, they are not causes. They are outcomes which came about as a result of the violation of human rights and freedoms of Albanians in Macedonia, beginning with their expulsion or being -- beginning with their being left out of the constitution of 1991; being described as non-constituent elements; and, in continuum, using the police against them in Bit Pazar, for example; or their refusal to have a pedagogical --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I apologise, may I interrupt you?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked me, and I am supposed to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I think I asked a straightforward question so I expect a brief answer.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can repeat your question. I'm very well familiar with the book. Ask me the question in that way so that it requires a short answer from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Are there many things in that book that are untrue, in your opinion, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say "yes" or "no" to your question, but I might have divided it in this way. The political part of the book is full of untruths when it comes to the part that speaks about the possibilities for mobilisation where the authors refer to the diary of the General Staff of the RA and all these things, than they refer to facts. I cannot -- army can say anything against that part [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And when they described the NLA as a gang of criminals and terrorists, is that correct? Is that part correct, that part of the book?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, no. It cannot be correct and true. They not only describe the NLA as a gang, as you are saying, but this is a description they apply to the entire Albanian population in Macedonia as a backward hostile population that doesn't like the Republic of Macedonia, then they say this is the fault of the government that has allowed the emergence of Albanian political parties and allowed them to act in this way and so on. For a book which has about 300 pages --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [No interpretation] ?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allow me to finish my question [as interpretation], please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I just intervene, sir. You are making what is essentially now a very extensive political speech, rather than answering a fairly confined question. The question can be answered shortly, giving the essence of what you're saying, without having to give the full detail, and I think it would help our timing and help the progress of the questioning if you were able to do that. Now, that will not deny you the opportunity of giving the essence of your view about a matter, but it will mean that you need not go into any full and expansive development whenever you're asked a relatively straightforward question, which is what is happening at the moment. So, please, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. I'll try to do as you are instructing me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I would go back to the issues related to the NLA disarmament and its stash of weapons. Is it correct that all NLA members were disarmed in the Operation Harvest organised by NATO?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, yes, even though the conditions were difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And when you say "disarmament," you refer to the weapons that the NLA members surrendered.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did the NLA members surrender also their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not. The Essential Harvest aimed only at collecting weapons, not uniforms; and, if they did so, they ought to be left without anything on.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Your organisation, the NLA, was not the signatory to the Ohrid political agreement. The signatories were the Macedonian and Albanian politicians. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Imer Imeri from the PDP and Arben Xhaferi from the DPA were the signatories to the Ohrid Framework Agreement as representatives of the Albanian parties?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But they were not representing the organisation, NLA. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the Prizren agreement, they represented also the NLA and its opinion. They kept constant contact with its political leader.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that Arben Xhaferi was the president of the DPA in 2001, while Menduh Thaci was the vice-president of DPA?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Arben Xhaferi, I remember him as the chairman of Democratic Party of Albanians, and I don't know who the deputy chairman was.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You stated that you had meetings with the representatives of the Albanian parties, and they fully supported your organisation, the NLA. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They signed the Ohrid Framework Agreement, and I'm testifying, based on this agreement, because they supported the NLA demands.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: They supported you also in terms of the means by which you wanted to achieve your goals, greater rights for the Albanian in Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which means are you talking about? I am not clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: They supported you also in the way -- regarding the way in which you wanted to achieve your goals, greater rights for the Albanian in Macedonia, through an uprising?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When meetings started, the uprising was ongoing, and the NLA - at least the way I know it - was fighting on the ground. Based on the contacts I had with it, we came up to the Prizren agreement. They didn't deny our demands but signed the Prizren agreement, which embodied a common stand on the political actions of these parties and of the NLA in the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did they support your uprising?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since they signed an agreement with us, of course they did, because it was supported by the entire population.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 65 ter 2D415.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This is a statement by Menduh Thaci, vice-president of the DPA, in 2001; published in the Dnevnik daily newspaper on the 30th of January 2007. The English translation is a draft translation organised by the Defence. And it states: "I learned informally that the anonymous Kosovar, in the meeting between Xhaferi, Dzindzik, Georgievski, was Hasim Taci. But, of course, he is not mentioning his name because this could have lasting consequences on Ahmeti. The partition of Macedonia is promised in the first -- five communiques of NLA, whose commander was Ahmeti. In the conversation, we had myself, Arben Xhaferi Musa Xhaferi, and Ali Ahmeti. He insisted that we that the Albanians should organise a little bit more, and they should take the wheat barn, Pelagonija; and then we should separate from Macedonia and destroy the state. "'He will have seriously prepare to be held responsible for the court for slander,' Thaci said. Regarding Thaci's accusation that VRMO-DPMNE and DPA are advocating the division of Macedonia, the deputy president of the DPA says: 'Ahmeti is threatening with another war. If he wishes to try yet another adventure of that kind, he will face a fierce response of the Albanians in Macedonia, Kosovo, and Albania.' "'The culprit for the victims we suffered is Ali Ahmeti,' accused Thaci."

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You didn't tell me where you were reading from, so that I could trade for myself because I know Macedonian. The interpreter didn't read everything because you were reading very fast. So can you please indicate to me where you were reading from, so that I can read it for myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: It starts with: "I understood informally." [Macedonian spoken]. It is in on the lower part of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we zoom in on the lower part of the page, and now towards the middle of the page.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you zoom it in, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Have you read the text?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which year is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This is 30th of January, 2007, and it speaks about the events in 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: From my understanding of the reading that my learned colleague has just put forward, with regards to the meeting that Ali Ahmeti had, I don't think that it's quite clear whether the meeting took place in 2001 or in 2007, at least from the reading that I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you allow me -- if you would allow me to continue asking my questions, it will become clearer, since my next question would show the witness the upper part of the document, which starts with: "The adventure of the private gang of Ali Ahmeti of 2001."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is your question? What are you asking me about? Can you please ask the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not receiving the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it clear from this that the DPA was not supporting you and the political parties were not supporting you in 2001, in your so-called uprising, which is the opposite of what you gave as your evidence?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is something that is done for political ends. This is a race between political parties. What this gentleman mentions here is, on one hand, he says what he says here; on the other hand, they work for the solution during the campaign and now for submitting a war on -- a law on the war veterans, the families of the martyrs. There is a disagreement between what he says and what he actually does. I don't know what to say with respect to this are you putting me. Ali Ahmeti is no longer the leader of the NLA. He is a chairman of a political party in the Republic of Macedonia, and the political fight among parties goes on.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, would this be the convenient time for the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We resume at five past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I was afraid something was happening behind me. I was wondering what was going on. Can the witness please be shown 65 ter 2945 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 2D415.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness Ostreni, regarding the events in 2001, Mr. Menduh Thaci says that...

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you can focus on the upper part.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: ... that: "This was an adventure of the private company of Ali Ahmeti in 2001, which resulted in the document for Kosovo." Now the word "independence" does not appear. "... Accused yesterday, Menduh Thaci, deputy president of the DPA. He announced that the leader of the DPA, Arben Xhaferi, will sue Ahmeti for defamation published in the interview in Dnevnik daily. That Xhaferi, Ljubco Georgievski, Zoran Djindjic, and the representative from Kosovo discussed the partition of the region in 2001. Thaci yesterday stated that Ahmeti is the one who wanted to partition Macedonia." Is it correct, Witness Ostreni, that your organisation, the NLA, did not have the support of the Albanian political party DPA in 2001 and from other Albanians as well?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not true. I don't agree with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it also correct that the goal of your organisation, led by Ahmeti, wanted to partition Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Your evidence is that you staged an uprising for rights and for changing the constitution of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never said that I staged this uprising. I only said that I joined it in order to contribute to the realisation of the rights and freedoms of the Albanians in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek to tender document 65 ter 2D415 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will object on the basis that this witness has not -- has no knowledge and, actually, didn't confirm the veracity and accuracy what is written in this document. Basically, that the Albanian political parties didn't support the NLA, and also that the aim of the NLA was the partition of Macedonia. He cannot testify on the accuracy and veracity of these statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness stated that his organisation, the NLA, had the support from the Albanian political parties in 2001, and the text here shows that this is contrary to the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The document will not be received, Mr. Apostolski. If you want to show what the views of critical people or organisations were in 2001, you may need to call those, rather than some press announcement in 2007 in a very political context.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness Ostreni, on page 47605 [as interpreted] of this transcript of 12th November, 2007, you stated that the ambassador of the United Kingdom supported you, and he said that he would feel insulted if he were an Albanian living in Macedonia. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say in 2007; I said in 2001. That statement is published in the Fakti newspaper, and it can carries also a photo of the distinguished ambassador.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The ambassador of the United Kingdom, in the Republic of Macedonia, in 2001, was Mark Dickinson. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember his name. I only know that it was published in Fakti along with his photo, and you can check it out with that newspaper. I have it in my computer, but I am here in the quality of a witness and have to resort to my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the witness can please be shown 2D71, Exhibit 2D71. It's a video-clip. This is an interview with Mr. Mark Dickinson, Ambassador of the United Kingdom to the Republic of Macedonia, in 2001. Can we please play it from the beginning. This interview is led in the English language, and it has subtitles in Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We seem to have no sound.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please go to the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The interview is given at the beginning of May 2001, after the killing of eight members of the Macedonian security forces in Vejce.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that, in effect, your organisation, the NLA, did not have the support of the ambassador of the United Kingdom, which is contrary to your evidence?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If what is published in the Fakti newspaper is wrong, then I'm wrong, too. I have the newspaper, and you can check it out with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But from this statement, it is clearly evident that the ambassador points to the fact that the NLA does not have the support of the Albanian population. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not deny what Mr. Ambassador is saying. I mean, this is what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have another question for this witness. It would be more of a general nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, according to you, if a given country, a people, do not believe that they're not entitled to rights, they do not have certain rights, an uprising would achieve the goal of gaining these rights and changing the constitution.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that it would achieve its right, but the uprising is a fact, and we have to analyse the causes that led to it. It ended with the signing of the Ohrid Framework Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Would it be -- since you know the situation in Kosovo, would it be in good order if the rights of the Serbs were not respected, that they should stage an uprising. Would you justify this?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me a question and ask me to comment on it. I don't know if I should do that, Your Honours. I think that all the citizens of Kosova should be guaranteed equal rights and not be given any cause for an uprising by anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But you justify the force as a means for gaining a certain right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that my colleague is putting some words in the mouth of this witness that he didn't testify about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Once again, that may well be true, Ms. Regue, but I doubt very much whether words could be put into the mouth of this witness by anyone. He knows well how to express his view. Carry on, Mr. Apostolski, but you may, in fact, have been suggesting answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you respond to my previous question?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat it? I'm afraid I don't remember it very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you justify the use of force as a means for realisation of rights?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I do not justify it, and I think that attainment of rights should be done in a democratic way. I believe that every state should do its duty to abide by international norms and by Euro-Atlantic standards, so that things do not come to that serious state.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Since you know well the constitution of the Republic of Macedonia, is it correct that in order to change the constitution of the Republic of Macedonia, it is sufficient that initiative of that kind be submitted by 150.000 citizens, that this is a lawful procedure by which they can initiate a change in the constitution?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Firstly, I want to say that I'm not very well familiar with the constitution of Macedonia, because I'm not a lawyer by profession. Secondly, I can't to say that when the Republic of Macedonia constitution was submitted to parliament for approval, the Albanian members didn't vote in favour it - it was in 1991 - because it was discriminating the Albanians. And whenever issues were put forward for solutions to democraticise the life and guarantee freedoms and rights of the Albanians, the Albanian deputies in parliament were outvoted by the Macedonian members. Therefore, the process developed as it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Were you a member of parliament from 2002 to 2006? Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And you said that there was a proposal for passing a law on pension for NLA fighters. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not at that time. The proposal was made recently. I don't recall that a proposal was actually made. There were attempts made, but not an actual proposal. Only now a proposal has been put in place, and it has been seen also by the European Union -- or it was seen in context of European Union standards, and it is expected to be discussed further.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Although, for four years, your party was in power together with the SDSM political party, you did not initiate this question and you did not pass this law, by which, as you also said, would serve as yet another confirmation that this was a regular and proper army?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not agree with the word you put to me, "your army," and as a "regular" army, because they are former members or soldiers of the NLA which was disarmed and demobilised, and that efforts are being made to employ these people in the Republic of Macedonia. At that time that we were in power, the Democratic Union for Integrity, we tried to table important draft laws in conformity with Ohrid Agreement and the constitution. Actually, we tabled a large number of proposals, but this law -- this draft was not submitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness Ostreni, for your comprehensive answers to my questions. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps I did not keep my promise that I would finish with this witness by the end of the first session, but I believe I'm only a little bit in delay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Apostolski. Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I believe that my colleague from the Defence wanted to tender the documents, or we can do it at the end, as Your Honour wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You remind me. Thank you for that matter. Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, and thank you to Ms. Regue. Your Honour, there is approximately ten or 11 documents which we would seek to tender. The first such documents was Rule 65 ter 1D1044. This is a document which was received from an embassy here in The Hague, and it comes from the department of defence of that particular country. The date of the document, then, is the 27th of June of 2001, and it talks in particular of two issues which we put to the witness. The first one was a statement contained in this document that the NLA group hid out in predominantly Albanian villages surrounding Skopje. The other aspect of this document which was put to the witness was the structure, organisation, and operational aspects of the organisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will object to this proposal, first because the witness didn't corroborate the content of the document. He cannot testify to the accuracy and the veracity. And, Your Honour, if we read actually the first paragraph of this document, it says: "Warning: This is an information report, not finally evaluated intelligence." That also brings some question about the reliability of the information contained in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps, briefly, Your Honour, if I may. I think the second issue is a fair one, if I may say so, by the Prosecution that it may indeed be an issue of weight since the author of that document has not been called, but that would be the case, Your Honour, with respect of any such document, including many tendered by the Prosecution. Considering -- concerning, I apologise, the first point, the absence of corroboration by the witness, this is the very point of tendering this document, Your Honour. This document, which was provided to us, shows what we believe was the reality of the situation at the time within the NLA, and one which we say is contrary to the evidence given by this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can I ask: Are you seeking to tender this document as proof of the truth of its content, or merely because it was a document that you put to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps the answer is twofold. We've indicated some difficulties at the beginning of the evidence of this witness, in particular in regard to obtaining information as pertain to the internal functioning of the organisation. We believe this document to be reliable because of the origin of that document. We also believe, having put other documents to the witness, including a Jane's article, including through Mr. Bezruchenko a report of ICJ and similar report, that this -- the information which is contained in that document is reliable, perhaps not on its own, but that it is corroborated and is corroborative of other information that has been led in this trial. So to answer your question, we would, in fact, seek to tender this document both in regard to the truth of its content as regard the organisation of the organisation, and in relation to the credibility, or otherwise, of the evidence given by the witness on that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber has had some discussion about this matter, Mr. Mettraux, because there are some fairly fundamental lines of principle that have to be considered, and it may be that we have not been entirely consistent throughout the trial in respect to some of these, because the issues are sometimes presented quite differently with quite different degrees of reaction by the witness to the content of the document. But in a case such as the present, the Chamber is persuaded that the proper course to follow is not to receive this document. It is a document, although coming from the records of a government which was actively involved in the region, where the creator of the document and the sources used by the creator are entirely unknown. So to use the document itself of proof of facts, in the Chamber's view, is getting beyond a matter of mere weight. It's getting to the point where this is just no demonstrative basis for reliability sufficient to justify its admission. Insofar as its content as being the subject to a specific comment in evidence by the witness, that is entirely and fully produced in the transcript record of that questioning, so that the document itself does not take the matter further. So, in those circumstances, and for the reasons briefly indicated, we would not receive this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The next document which we will seek to tender is Rule 65 ter 1D116. Your Honour will recall this is a statement made by the President of the United States, George W. Bush, on the 14th of August of 2001, and it followed a telephone conversation which President Bush had with President Trajkovski. The document was put to the witness in relation to two particular matter. One was the evidence given by the witness about the significance, in particular, of the Ohrid Framework Agreement. A proposition was put to him that, contrary to the suggestion of putting an end to a conflict, the Ohrid Framework Agreement was actually one to avert a war, which is the content of this document. The other matter to which we say this document is or may be relevant is insofar as it is another indication of state practice, insofar as the circumstances of what was happening in the Republic of Macedonia is concerned, in particular, as regard the fact that this document, as many others, indicate the view that the NLA was never regarded as being a party to an armed conflict or that the situation in the area was, in fact, an armed conflict, but instead contains evidence of condemnation of the activities and crimes and tactics by the president of the United States. We would tender it, in -- for those reasons, and Your Honour it was obtained, we believe, from the official web site of the American Presidency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, we will object on the basis that my colleague has mentioned it was put to the witness, the issue of the -- of the civil war, but the witness cannot actually testify and cannot corroborate the veracity of this document, as he actually testified on the contrary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So you dispute that this is a record of a statement made by the president. Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I dispute that the witness cannot -- the witness basically didn't testify -- didn't -- on the content or the accuracy of the statement, which is within in the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: In this case, the Chamber will receive this document, Mr. Mettraux. The circumstances of this case make it relevant to at least some degree what views were held by nations of the world at the relevant time, and this is one apparent source for such view, concerning one nation. There is a sufficient apparent authenticity about the nature and source of the document to justify its admission. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D265, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next document which the Defence would seek to tender is Rule 65 ter 1D705. This is the record of a meeting of the General Assembly of the United Nations, in the month of November of 2001. It is entitled, "Press release, GA," for General Assembly,"9962." The record of this meeting was put to the witness, more specifically the statement given to the general assembly by the then Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Macedonia, and the document was put to the witness in at least two respect or in relation to two particular issues. One was the view taken by the Macedonian government through its representative, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, about the status of the NLA, and you will recall that the activities of the NLA was characterised as terrorist attacks. The other matter to which the document was used was in relation, again, to the Ohrid Framework Agreement, where the minister, contrary, we submit, to the evidence given by the witness, made it clear that the Ohrid Framework Agreement had, in fact, been an accord reached by political parties with a view to isolate the NLA and not in any way to give any legitimacy to their activities. There are several reference again to the NLA being a terrorist group or its activities being characterised as terrorist activities, which in itself might be relevant, we submit, to the issue of the armed conflict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is it a document of 11 pages, and actually two paragraphs were only put to the witness, which, indeed, are the two paragraphs which are in the record and deal with the statement of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Macedonia. Again, the witness -- the witness, again, with cannot testify, cannot corroborate the veracity of this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honours, perhaps, a very, very brief reply in relation to this. I believe the first page was also put to the witness, and it may be important, Your Honours, since it contains, if you wish, the summary of the entire debate; and then I turned to the part, as my colleague indicated, which is the statement of the minister.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This document will be received. The essential reasoning is that indicated in respect of the previous.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will become Exhibit 1D266, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The next document is Rule 65 ter 1D956. This document, Your Honour, is a press statement which comes from the official web site of the US Department of State. It is dated 28th of April of 2001, and it refers to -- I will read the title: "US condemns attack on eight Macedonian soldiers by armed ethnic Albanian extremists." This document, Your Honour, you will recall, refers to an incident in or near the village of Vejce on the 28th of April of 2001, in which eight Macedonian members of the Armed Forces were killed. In our submission, Your Honour, this matter may be or is, in fact, of relevance to these proceedings. It has been discussed by Mr. Bezruchenko and also by the present witness, and is being characterised in terms of criminal acts and not in terms of legitimate military action. There are other documents which I have put to this witness and others which have already been admitted, which confirm the same view, and this, again, Your Honour, may be relevant or, in our submission, is relevant to the relevance, if any, that may be given to the incident in Vejce, as a matter pertaining to the alleged armed conflict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber will not receive this document, Mr. Mettraux, essentially, so far as it may have some relevance, it appears, in its material respects, adequately in the transcript, and the witness has commented in respect of those passages.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I am grateful to Your Honour. The next document will be Rule 65 ter 1D887. Your Honour, this is a document which, again, comes from the US Department of State. Its title is: "Europe overview pattern of global terrorism, 2000," and the date of that document is the 30th of April of 2001. Your Honour may recall that a similar document, although a much larger in scope, was put to a previous witness, and it was the same document, if you wish, but for 2002, which covered the rest of the year 2001. The passage which was put to this witness, in the course of his evidence, concern the suggestion by the State Department that the NLA had fired indiscriminately upon civilian centres. The reason for putting this document, this particular information to the witness was twofold: One, to establish the state of his knowledge, if any, about the activities within his organisation; and, secondly, the fact that orders, which the witness said were given to -- not hurt civilians in compliance with humanitarian law, were, in fact, being disregarded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is also a document which deals with issues related to different countries, and, indeed, it was put to the witness one single paragraph, and he had the opportunity to actually answer to that. He didn't corroborate the information which is in it. But my point is mainly that we are talking about one paragraph which was already put.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will not receive this document, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The next document would be -- I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise. The next document would be Rule 65 ter 1D1042. Your Honour, this is, again, a document such as the first one which was sought to be tendered, and which comes from the same governmental authorities and has the same sort of department of defence of that particular country. It is dated the 10th of July of 2001, and the material which was put to the witness in relation to that document is at the second page of this document. There are essentially three different types of facts or matters which are contained in that second page and which were put to the witness. The first one relates to the indiscriminate pre-cease-fire mortar attacks by the NLA on Tetovo. The second one is a list of crimes allegedly committed by the NLA which are listed in this document, in particular in the area in or around Tetovo. The third part of the paragraph in question concern the fact that -- concerns are expressed in that document that Ali Ahmeti may not be firmly in control of this renegade cell or cells and continued cease-fires violations from this group can be expected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, fist, I will also mention that the same warning which is in the previous document is there. Therefore, we will also challenge the reliability of the document in this point and the veracity of the information contained in it. And, again, Your Honour, the source of the information is not established neither in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This document will not be received as indicated for the first document sought to be tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The next document would be Rule 65 ter 1D1025, and this is a so-called "spot report" by the OSCE. It's dated the 25th of July of 2001. It records the fact that the ethnic Albanian armed group is threatening people in both Jegunovce and Vratnica, and also the fact that villagers are being told to leave or risk being shot. It comes from the OSCE, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that the witness had no knowledge about -- about these facts as he testified; and, therefore, the veracity of the information was not established.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The evidence that has been given, although it seem as long time ago now in this trial, concerning the manner of preparation of OSCE reports of this nature and the degree of cross-references and confirmation given to them, provides, in the Chamber's present assessment, a basis upon which a report of this nature may be accepted as possibly and apparently more reliable than a document such as the intelligence reports which have been offered to us. Now, that being so, there is a justification which brings this document into the category of sufficiently reliable to justify admission. That having been said, we wish to make it clear that we are not, by admitting the document, indicating that we would, in the end, attach to it, in respect of any disputed content, an accepted reliability in our own assessment. But we are simply trying to determine whether there is a sufficient reliability of the document to be admitted. In view of the specific evidence about reports of that nature, we will receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D267, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Your Honour. The next document is Rule 65 ter 1D1282. This is, again, a document from the OSCE, this one dated 29 August 2001, and this is a so-called OSCE "spillover monitor mission" to Skopje. It comes, I believe, from the secretariat. The document -- or the part of the document which was put to the witness concerned and related to the issue of the use of religious facilities as military emplacement and the destruction of such properties. The number -- I apologise, Your Honour, the 65 ter number would be 1D828.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D268, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next document is offered for the same basis and for the same reason as the document of the American Presidency. This one is a statement by the Russian Foreign Ministry, through its official spokesman of the 26th June 2001. This is Rule 65 ter 1D438. It is dated, as I mentioned, the 26 June 2001, and it refers to the activities of the NLA at that time, and also records the view of the Russian authorities about the status of the NLA as a terrorist group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This document will be received. Can it be clear, in view of something you have just said, Mr. Mettraux, that this, like Exhibit 1D265, is received not as evidence of the truth of its contents, but as evidence that the government of a nation of the world expressed a view about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we understand this, and this is also the main purpose behind the tendering of the document. It is to show that, as far as the state concerns, expressed their view in various documents. Those views may be reflect in the document that we are now seeking to tender.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will become Exhibit 1D269, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, the same -- I believe the same submission and the same caveat would apply to the next document, which is Rule 65 ter 1D715, which is a statement by the press secretary of the White House. It is dated the 27th of June of 2001. Your Honour will recall that a number of issues were addressed through this document, in particular, the withdrawal of the NLA from Aracinovo, the fact that the activities of the NLA were again characterised as terrorist violence, and also reference was made to certain restrictive measures that were applied on to the NLA and members of that organisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D270, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
