utterances.text: The next document, Your Honour, and perhaps with the same introduction, is again is Rule 65 ter 1D889. This is a so-called "joint statement of the Ministers of Foreign Affairs of the south-east European Cooperation Process," and it is dated the 16th of May of 2001 in Tirana. It's part of the stability pact for south-eastern Europe. The passage which was read out to the witness, contained in this statement, pertains to the view expressed by the foreign ministers of the countries of the south-eastern part of the Balkans, that the activities of the NLA were to be regarded as terrorist activities and the NLA itself as an Albanian extremist group. There was also a call being made for the release of hostages, which is another issue that touched upon with this witness, and a reference to the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the republic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D2771, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document, Your Honour - and I think there is an agreement with the Prosecution on this particular document - this was Rule 65 ter 317 from the Prosecution Rule 65 ter list. This is an order signed by the then Chief of Staff of the army, General Pande Petrovski, dated the 5th of July of 2001, in which he ordered a cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D272, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And Your Honour, perhaps as a matter of clarification, you will recall that at the end of the cross-examination, questions were asked about the origin of a particular document, and we had indicated that it came from the EUMM. It appears to be correct, and my colleague had asked about the date of that particular document. The document was actually listed on the Rule 65 ter list of the Prosecution, and it appears as an undated document and we have not been otherwise to establish the date of that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General Ostreni, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, you were asked about the fact that you were given the rank of general upon joining the NLA. I'd like to ask you on which basis were the ranks awarded to the different NLA members. Which facts, if any, were taken into consideration when awarding the ranks.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the NLA, the personnel establishment determines the ranks. It was normal at that time, in determining their rank, to include their abilities, their experience with wars, and the way they carried out their duties and, of course, the post that they held.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: When you refer to "experience with wars," could you be please be a bit more clearer on that point?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the NLA, there were members who had participated in the Kosova war, and were -- had joined the uprising from the very beginning, the uprising that turned into National Liberation Army, and the post that they were gradually promoted to during carrying out their tasks and, of course, their capacities and abilities in their personal lives.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: What do you mean "with their capacities and abilities in their personal life."

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their education that they had completed.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, you were also asked about the appointment of Ali Ahmeti, and who appointed Ali Ahmeti as supreme commander of the NLA. General, do you know who appointed, who elected Fidel Castro in as the leader of the uprising movement in Cuba in 1959, who defeated Batista?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about Cuba, but the comrades that he cooperated with accepted him as their leader; and when I joined the NLA, I accepted Ali Ahmeti as my leader, and I accepted to follow his orders as of the time that I was appointed Chief of the General Staff of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, you were also asked, yesterday I believe, and I quote: "Whether, when you joined the NLA, you had the impression that this organisation existed earlier." You were required a yes or no answer. Your answer was, and I quote again: "No. My impression was that there was a ongoing uprising, and that I should give my contribution to the Albanians to whom I belong in the Republic of Macedonia." General, who was leading this uprising prior to March 2001, if you know?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I don't know. When I arrived, I met Mr. Ali Ahmeti, and we talked. He explained that there was an on going uprising. He proposed what I already stated, and, consequently, I accepted the post. But, as I stated earlier, I was ready to join ranks of the NLA as an ordinary soldier, because I wanted to contribute to what was going on to my people in my own country.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Therefore, General, in March, when you met with Ali Ahmeti, who was leading the uprising at that time?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. My impression was that Ali Ahmeti was aware of what was going on. He was familiar with the people around him, and that was enough information for me at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If the registry could please call Exhibit 1D00227?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, this is a --

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And if we could focus to the first part in the bottom of the document, just below the title: "Will Macedonia be next?"

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, This was a document which was shown to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: The first paragraph below this. Yeah, perfect, here. Thanks a lot.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, I'm afraid that it's in English, this document, so I will read it to you. This is a document produced by the Jane's Intelligence Digest in the 2nd of February 2001. In the first paragraph, it reads, and I quote: "In the space of a week, ethnic Albanian terrorists have launched an attack on a Macedonian police station."

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And if we could please go to the second page and focus on the third full paragraph, which start with "The low level attacks."

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, this document reads that: "The low level attacks against the Macedonian police, which began last year," meaning 2000 "are supposedly the work of the so-called Liberation Army, four of whom have been arrested." General, according to this document, did the NLA start operating against police forces as early as 2000?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This I don't know. At the time, I was the Chief of General Staff of KPC in Kosovo, and I carried those duties with full responsibility. I don't know if you mentioned the date of this document, but this document refers to a period of time when I was not there, when I was in the United States, and was not following closely the situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General. The date was the 2nd of February, 2001, and it was referring to events occurring in January of 2001 and also 2000.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could please call Exhibit P45, which is the "White Book," and if we could go to page 111th, in the English version and 57 in the Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, you will see on the right side of the screen the Macedonian version. Just wait a second.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Maybe we can focus a little bit the Macedonian so it's clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, this document bears the title: "Terrorist attacks and provocations carried out by the so-called NLA." The first events is recorded on the 11th of January of 2000, and it reads: "At the entry of the village of Aracinovo, during the armed attack against the police patrol of the Ministry of Interior, three police officers were killed. "By a communique presented on January 30th, 2000, the responsibility for this terrorist attack was claimed by the so-called NLA." Then the second event recorded in this page refers to the 19th of January of 2000: "The police station, Oslomej-Kicevo, was attacked by a mortar grenade launcher." The third event refers to the 22nd of January 2001: "The police station, Tearce, Tetovo, was attacked by a hand-grenade mortar and an automatic weapon and was hit with two projectiles. A police officer was killed." And then the document reads: "By a communique number 4, presented on January 23, 2001, NLA took the responsibility for this attack." The next event recorded in this page, General, it's the 2nd of February and it should read 2001, I believe, because the events are recorded in chronological order: "The building of the department of internal affairs Kumanovo was attacked with a hand bomb." The last event recorded, it is dated 16th of February, 2001, and, indeed, you referred to this event in your evidence, General, and I quote: "In the vicinity of the village of Tanusevci, Skopje, a journalist team of the A1 television from Skopje was captured by armed members of the NLA."

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It is not an objection, just a clarification. It would appear that the year 2nd February is 2000 in the Macedonia only; not 2001 as indicated.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I was aware of that. Thanks a lot, Mr. Mettraux. But as the events are recorded in a chronological order, I assumed, wrongly or not, that there was a mistake in the original version.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, this second page, and I won't go over these events, refer to some NLA operations/actions carried out already in March 2001. General, would you agree that, according to the Ministry of Interior who actually produced this document, actions carried out by the NLA already took place as early as 2000?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The persons that worked on the Law on Amnesty have not made the beginning date of the persons that would be amnestied, and they have put an end date, which is after the demobilisation. But since these events are listed here, maybe they happened in reality. Again, I would like to mention that until March 2000, I was in the area of Dukagjini; and on 1st of March -- or 3rd, 4th March, I accepted the post of the Chief of Staff of the KPC in Kosovo, and then I went on holiday. So I wasn't closely following the developments on the ground before I joined the NLA. After the 14th, that is, on the 19th and 20th of March, I was in Vejce. That's when I started to tour the terrain. As for other dates, I cannot ascertain their accuracy. I know that there is this "White Book." I don't know how things developed. This is how events are listed in the book. But who made the entries and on basis of what information, that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could please go to pages 341 of the "White Book" in English and 167 in Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Again, General, we are going to look at another several pages from the "White Book," in particular, this chapter which bears the title: "Selected communique by the so-called NLA."

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: The Macedonian should be page 167. Now it will be -- the corresponding Macedonian page would be 168, if we could go. Thanks a lot.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, you will be able to see the Macedonian text on the right side of your screen. General, this is a communique issued by the NLA on January 30, 2000, and I'm just going to read to you the first paragraph: "We informed the public that we have committed the military attacks in January near Skopje, when Macedonian policemen were killed, and in Oslomej near Kicevo, when the police station was damaged." General, would you agree that based on this document, the NLA was claiming that that had already committed actions, perpetrated actions as early as January 2000?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness could be asked first whether he know this is document, or whether he has seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I believe that, in cross-examination, the witness already answered that he had not seen any communique prior to him joining. But, if Your Honour wish, I can ask him whether he has seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. As far as I recall, the witness gave evidence to the effect that he does not know the content of the first communiques, and that the first one he was aware of was communique number 6 of the month of March 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, my question was: If, based on the document that you have in front of you, you can see, you can read that the NLA, as early as January 30, 2000, already claimed that the organisation had perpetrated actions in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what the document says. Maybe someone drafted this document, but personally I did not take part in this work, and I didn't know of the communiques prior to communique number 6. As of this communique and the following ones, those I can recognise and I can testify to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks a lot. I'm just going to show you another communique.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could please turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: This was a communique mentioned by my colleague, Mr. Mettraux, in his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Simply to indicate for the transcript, Your Honour, that we asked questions, general questions about the communique number 4, and that the witness indicated he had not seen it and didn't know of its content, and the matter was left at that in view of his evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, this communique is it dated the 23rd of January, 2001, and reads: "Communique number 4: Yesterday, January 22, 2001, in Tearce near Tetovo, a special unit of the National Liberation Army, supported by a group of monitors, attack the Macedonian police station using automatic rifles and hand-grenade launchers." General, is this document stating that in the -- in January 22nd, 2001, an action was already perpetrated by the NLA in Tearce near Tetovo?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please enlarge the document? Are we talking about communique number 4 here.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, General. I believe it is the one that you have.

utterances.speaker: MR. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks a lot, to the registry.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I was reading the first three lines of the document, General.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of communique number 4?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, General.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first two lines are of the body that drafted the book, if we're talking of the same document, with number 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Sorry, General. Maybe I will rephrase my question because I didn't quite understand your answer. I was simply asking that, based on this document which was included within the "White Book," the NLA already claim, as of January 22nd, 2001, the commission, the perpetration of some actions in Tearce near Tetovo. That was my only question, General.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have communique number 4 before me, but not all of it, so that can I read it fully and give you my views on it. In the screen before me, there's only part of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before you do that, Mr. Ostreni, can I point out that, on the screen, there is both an English version and a Macedonian version with a heading "Communique number 4," but their content and date appears quite different. Perhaps it is that the witness is being asked to comment on a document which is different from the one you were reading in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We should, in the Macedonian version, we should move to the -- to the left, because we are -- that was my mistake. Thanks, Your Honour. If we could enlarge the upper part of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, I was referring to the communique number 4, dated 23rd of January, 2001, which you have in the upper part of the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise for interfering my colleague with the re-direct, but I believe that the witness was confused as well, because I speak the Macedonian language. The communique number 4, shown before, was related to a completely different event, and now the witness is, again, shown a communique number 4 dealing with yet another event, at least in the Macedonian version.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Well, I don't speak Macedonian, but I believe that the first line reads, "22nd of January."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we now may have the correct communique. It could be useful if this was looked at over the break, Ms. Regue, and make sure that the witness has the right document when we resume after the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: All right? We'll resume at five minutes past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, if could you please look, again, to the upper -- at the right side of your screen, the text which is in the upper part of the document. This communique, which bears the number 4, and is dated the 23rd of January, 2001, reads: "Yesterday, January 22, 2001, in Tearce near Tetovo, special unit of the NLA, supported by group of monitors, attacked the Macedonian police station using automatic rifles and hand-grenade launchers." My question was, General, if, based on this document, actions were already undertaken by the NLA as of January 22nd, 2001 in Tearce near Tetovo?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't present at that time, and I don't know. This is what it says here, and maybe it was so.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could please remove the document from the screen. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, did the NLA rules and regulations provide with disciplinary measures to be undertaken by the brigades?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The internal rules says, in one part, that in cases of breaches of discipline, people may be detained. That's the only one. That's the only one that is -- Article that is included there.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Why was important to have these measures in the regulations?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the brigade commanders should have the power to detain a soldier, in case of a breach of discipline in the NLA, because if there was no rules, he might ask the soldier to surrender the weapon and send him home. We couldn't do more than that because we didn't have a law to regulate the entire activity of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, it was put to you that the Ohrid Agreement averted a civil war, and you didn't agree with such a statement and testified that the Ohrid Agreement put an end to the war and was used to build a democratic Macedonia. General, about the structure, the organisation of the NLA by August 2001, I'd like to ask you some questions. Had the brigades established their authority over territories in Macedonia at that time?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The brigades were stationed in the way I have indicated in the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not -- may you ask the question more directly for me to give a more focussed answer?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I will ask you, please, to answer briefly; and if it is necessary, to provide also a brief explanation, General.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will give a brief explanation. At the time, the brigades were located in the places that we have marked in on the map we have submitted to NATO. Within these places, where there communes, they functioned. The NLA did not hinder in any way the operating, the functioning of such communes, and there are some statements to this effect issued by the chairman of the commune.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: But just to wrap it up, by August 2001, had the brigades established their authorities over the territories in this map that you exhibit to this Trial Chamber? It's a "yes" or "no" answer, General.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Had the brigades been assigned zones of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The maps show, in a way, the areas of responsibilities of brigades at the time when the cease-fire took effect, and this remained so until the signing of the Ohrid Agreement; in fact, until the disarmament of the NLA, its demilitarisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Had the General Staff and different brigades headquarters?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had their commands, and they have marked also in the map, depending on their size. You have the sign for the Brigade 113 command; then that of 112 in Sipkovica and so on; the 1st Battalion of Brigade 115 in Radusa; and the one in open air of Brigade 116; Brigade 114 at that time was in Kustak, but this is not shown here.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General. Were you Ali Ahmeti and yourself issuing military orders and recommendations to the brigade commanders? Again, General, if you could answer with a "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Were the brigade commanders issuing orders to the units subordinated to them?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I see my colleague is standing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, certainly, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would simply wish to indicate that, at this stage, we seem to be undertaking a new examination-in-chief, on which we will have no right to cross-examine. I think the those questions are quite important. And to the extent they are important to the Prosection as well, we believe they should have been asked in examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that, in examination-in-chief, these issues were already dealt with; and, in cross-examination, the issue of armed conflict was largely challenged by my colleagues, and I was trying to build up that point again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Continue, Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, I see you answered the last question. Were the brigade commanders reporting to you on daily basis?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were obliged to report in the morning and in the evening, and in cases of some states of unusual events.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Were the brigades following the NLA regulations, as well as the orders and instructions issued by the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Was the NLA able to supply to its brigades, battalions, basically to the different units, with weaponry and equipment?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: With difficulty, but yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Was the NLA by August 2001 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise to my colleague, but we really wish to make it, once again, clear for the transcript that those questions, to the extent that they would have been relevant to the Prosecution case, and to the extent that they were not explored in examination-in-chief, should have been done at that stage. Those questions, if relevant, had to be asked, in particular as regard the last questions about logistics.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If it be made clear also, Mr. Mettraux, that, in the view of the Chamber, the re-examination is being conducted properly, dealing, in a direct manner, with issues that were raised very extensively in particular, but not solely, by your own cross-examination. Carry on, please, Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, was the NLA recruiting new members by August 2001, meaning new members were joining the NLA by August 2001?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our attempt was not to expand it from the signing on the cease-fire. The reason was not to keep -- it was not reasonable to keep a large number of people, to feed them three times a day, to equip them with uniforms, and so on. We didn't want to expand, but I can't rule out that some volunteers joined the brigades, but not in August.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, about -- you testified about problems after the cease-fire with regards to both sides of the conflict. You also testified that there were provocations from the Macedonian security forces before the signing of the agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please call Exhibit P481, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, you will see in your screen, on the right side in Macedonian, a resolution issued by the president, Boris Trajkovski, on the 5th of August, 2001. If I may read the first paragraph, it says, and I quote: "The army of the Republic of Macedonia, with necessary structure and force, is to enter the town of Tetovo with the aim of preventing its fall into the hands of the terrorist groups of the self-styled NLA and protecting the lives, safety, and property of the citizens of Tetovo." General, were you aware of these measures undertaken by President Trajkovski in August 2001?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A similar order was published also in the media on the 5th of August, something which greatly worried all of us in the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Which consequences, if any, had for the NLA these measures undertaken by the president?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the head of the state, or the supreme commander, decides to undertake an operation at the time of the cease-fire, eight days prior to the signing of the Ohrid Agreement and this is published in the media, it is understandable that this causes concern, because we are afraid that the political agreement wouldn't be respected -- wouldn't be signed and that the question arose as to the conflict continuing.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please -- could we please call 65 ter 284, and if we could go to the page 8, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And, General, in the meantime that we wait for this new document, were you aware of fighting going on in Tetovo that August 2001?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay. I will move on to the next issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If he could please remove this document from the screen, I would be grateful.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, it was put to that you the NLA did not have a centralised command system and a General Staff was militarily irrelevant. You testified that Ali Ahmeti, as well as NATO and European Union representatives, negotiated and agree the withdrawal on the 24th of June, 2001. Which brigade was in Aracinovo at that time?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 24th of June, there was part of Brigade 113 in Haracin. There was a battalion that was withdrawn from there on the order of Ali Ahmeti.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: So, General, if I can follow up on your answer, once Ali Ahmeti reached the agreement with the international representatives, to whom did he issue, to whom did he communicate the order to withdraw within the structure of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He gave the order to Brigade 113, after consulting with me as well, because at the time I was in Prizren, while Mr. Ali Ahmeti was in Shipkovice.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Was this order followed by the Brigade 113?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The battalion and its units withdrew from Haracin, I think on the 25th.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, once the brigade commander received the order to withdraw, to whom did he communicate the order within the 113th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the commander who was in Haracin. However, I cannot rule out the possibility of Mr. Ali Ahmeti talking with the leader who was in Haracin, but I have no information. I only know that this was discussed with the brigade. I, too, discussed this with the brigade commander, but not -- I didn't discuss the withdrawal. I discussed prior and during the talks. I also discussed with Mr. Ali Ahmeti.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: You answered: "To the commander who was in Aracinovo." Did you mean the commander of the 113th Brigade or the commander of the battalion who was in Aracinovo?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean the brigade commander, Brigade 113.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And did the commander of the Brigade 113 issue any order to his units with regards to this matter?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He issued an order, and then the withdrawal took place with the presence or contribution of the internationals.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could please call Exhibit P498, and go to page 31, please. P498, page 31. I believe this is not Exhibit P498, which are the "Rules of Service of the NLA." It's former 65 ter 778.4, if we could go to page 31, please. Yes, this is the right page in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, chapter 5 of the Rules of Service reads: "The tasks of persons in positions of authority," and it starts with the commander of the unit, the commander of (detachment). To which commander this Article is referring to?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's referring to the brigade, in this case, commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: In item 1, it reads: "A unit (detachment) commander is in command ever all unit (detachment) troops under his direction and is the immediate commander of servicemen directly subordinated to him. He shall carry out his tasks pursuant to laws and by-laws of the orders issued by the NLA commander ..." General, in the case of Aracinovo, did the commander of the 113th Brigade proceed to withdraw following the order of the commander, Ali Ahmeti?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could remove the document from the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, you also testified that Ali Ahmeti and NATO representatives reached agreement with regard to the so-called operation or plan Harvest.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please show Exhibit P517.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, in the meantime that we wait for the document, was the militarisation of the NLA carried out according to the operation to the operation, to the plan Harvest?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, fully, in compliance with the plan. It even exceeded what was foreseen in the plan in terms of the number of weapons collected.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, you testified that this document, it was an instruction or recommendation to the brigades to prepare for the surrender of the weapons. To your knowledge, did they follow your instruction?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see here the document. They did follow my instructions, and the handing in of weapons was concluded successfully.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please show on the screen Exhibit 2D56.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, do you know these people, or at least some of the people, which appear in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know some of them: Number 5, Ali Ahmeti --

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Please wait one moment, General, for my learned colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that Defence did not use this photograph in the cross-examination, so I see no reason why the Prosecution would use it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, Your Honour. I'm dealing with an issue which was raised within cross-examination, despite that this photo was not shown, if I can procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The nature of the issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Clothing, uniforms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, you mentioned that you know some of these people, but I would like to ask you, first of all: What are these people wearing? What sort of clothing are they wearing?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Various uniforms; camouflage uniforms; a T-shirt which is part of the uniform; one is in black clothes; one is in black vest.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: The green T-shirt, was it part of the uniform of the NLA, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When we had it, we always handed it out to the soldiers as part of the uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Was it required to wear uniform in military operations, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. But in this photo, I see people just to take a photo with their commander, not that they are in any operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Why was it necessary, mandatory, to wear uniforms in military operations, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because that is part of an army. The uniform is suitable to use for work, part of which part of the work of a soldier is taking part in military operations. That distinguishes him from a civilian. After someone has taken a weapon, then the uniform is proof of showing that that person is a part of an organisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please show Exhibit 2D57.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, to your knowledge, if you do, in which context was this photo taken?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I see it, and judging from the terrain, it must be in the training centre of Brodec during the visit that Ali Ahmeti made there. You can see that some of the volunteers are not in uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: When the uniforms will be given to these new members, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we could get hold of the uniforms; and, at that moment they were also issued a weapon. You can see in the photo that they don't have weapons either.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, was the training mandatory, required, before start operating in the NLA?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Training was mandatory. It was a period during which the new -- newly conscripted soldiers, let say, didn't go immediately to the front, but get used. Even the formation of the brigades followed this rule. From the 13th was formed the 14th and so on; from the 15th, the 16th. The commander and myself took care to send to the front officers and soldiers who had already taken part in some fighting, and then other -- gradually other soldiers. That was the priority we followed. We didn't want someone who had not any experience of war be sent to the front line, because he would loose his life more easily.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: We can remove the photo from the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, it was also put to you that an example of the military relevance of the NLA was the fact that you did not provide to the OTP any written combat order, with the exception that the map and plan that we discussed earlier on. How were the combat orders issued to the brigade commander, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had satellite communication with all brigades and we also used mobile phones, but usually we used satellite phones to protect ourselves from being bugged. The commanders and the members of the brigade commands passed to -- passed by the General Staff and contacted directly with us. I have to stress this because, by the end, the NLA brigades extended from the border -- the northern border of the Republic of Macedonia to the vicinity of Debar. Therefore, it was indispensable for us to communicate through telephone, and also for them to contact us directly, to give us reports, to describe the situation in more details, and to get new tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, it was also put to you that you were not appointed as Chief of Staff before the 13th of May, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please see Exhibit P493, page 34. If we could please enlarge the paragraph where the name of the witness appears, which is the third one starting -- the one in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, I believe we have only an English version; therefore, I'm going to read to you what this document stated. This is a book with the title -- it's a book from NATO relating to the NLA, and it is dated the 25th of June 2005. This document reads General, that you became TMK, Chief of Staff, before suddenly departing and resurfacing with the NLA in April 2001. General, when did you join the NLA? In March, April, or May?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I joined the National Liberation Army in the month of March upon my return from the United States of America. I went back for a brief period to my work, and then I joined the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: When you were appointed Chief of Staff of the NLA, did you hold any public press conference to announce your appointment?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I signed a communique regarding the MX operation that was carried out in Tetovo on the 25th of March. After this operation, I went out public through this communique signed by me, explaining what happened there, and I believe you have this communique in the documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, would that be a convenient time, because I'm moving to a new topic and it may take some time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We adjourn and resume tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 15th day of November, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 25
